title: The answer was there. Did it get found?
hook: The knowledge base holds the answer. Does the model ever get to read it?

knows: that a chatbot can look things up in documents before answering
doesNotKnow: that only the top few retrieved passages reach the model
that keyword matching can rank the right passage below the cut

misconception: If the answer is in the knowledge base, the system will find it.
objective: The learner can explain that a retrieval-fed model answers only from the passages ranked above the cut, so a right passage that shares no words with the question can be invisible to it.

claims.text: Searching 'What is the capital of France?' by keywords (capital, France), 'Paris is the French seat of government.' scores 0 and the other four chunks score 1 each and tie; with ties kept in list order the top 2 are 'Rome is the capital of Italy.' and 'France exports a lot of wine.'
claims.source: wordScore() and ranking('words') in Demo.tsx (node output: scores 0,1,1,1,1; order 1,2,3,4,0). The tie-break rule is the toy's.

claims.text: The meaning scores are hand-set for the toy, not computed by an embedding model.
claims.source: CHUNKS[].meaning in Demo.tsx, chosen by the builder so that the Paris chunk ranks first; labelled in the reveal.

claims.text: Paris is the seat of the French government (the capital of France).
claims.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Paris'; Government of France (the 1958 Constitution does not name Paris, so it is not cited). · Fact-check 2026-10-13: Source is weak: the 1958 Constitution does not name Paris as capital; cite Encyclopaedia Britannica "Paris" or the Government of France instead.

claims.text: Retrieval-augmented systems pass the top-k retrieved passages to the model, and real systems use learned embeddings to match by meaning.
claims.source: About real systems: Lewis et al. 2020, 'Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks' (NeurIPS); Karpukhin et al. 2020, 'Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering' (EMNLP).

claims.text: In this setup the model answers only from what retrieval hands it: a right passage below the cut does not exist for it.
claims.source: Reveal paragraph 2. True of the toy and of a system that is given only the retrieved passages. Real retrieval-augmented models also carry knowledge in their weights (Lewis et al. 2020 call it parametric memory), so "only" overstates for real systems; suggest "answers from what retrieval hands it, in this setup". Added by fact-checker 2026-10-13; needs an independent check. DISPUTED 2026-10-13: 'The model answers only from what retrieval hands it' is true of the toy but the sentence follows a remark about real systems; real retrieval-augmented models also carry knowledge in their weights (Lewis et al. 2020, parametric memory, checked). Fix: 'In this setup the model answers only from what retrieval hands it'. | CLAIM FIX 2026-10-13: Was 'The model answers only from what retrieval hands it' (disputed: real retrieval-augmented models also carry parametric knowledge). Reveal now says 'in this setup'. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 4): Rechecked: reveal says 'in this setup the model answers only from what retrieval hands it'.

recall.question: A company chatbot answers from its help pages, but says it can't find the refund policy, which is on a page titled 'Returns'. What is the most likely cause?
options: The returns page was ranked below the passages handed to the model
The model refused to answer about money
The model forgot the page after reading it
recall.why: The model only reads the top few retrieved passages. A page that does not use the question's words can rank below the cut, and then the model never sees it.
